Guevara's experience of Latin America is his experience of oppression, which comes in multiple forms. Latin America is still living with the legacy of Spanish colonialism. This legacy is apparent everywhere, from churches, cities, and place names taken from Spanish conquerors. It informs the very language Ernesto Che Guevara uses to describe the people he meets across his Latin American travels. For example, terms such as _mestizo_ , _mulatto_ , and _Indian_ pepper Guevara's description of the people he meets, each time evoking the racial categories introduced to Latin America through Spanish colonialism. Such language and categories appear naturally in young Guevara's account of the world he inhabits, which shows how deeply entrenched such categories are even among people of
